limitations: This is a portal-token runtime acceptance sub-scope, not a complete manual caller/issuer review of the 202 authenticated-executable SECURITY DEFINER functions.
The 202-function allowlist remains blocked at 0/202 individually accepted; no entries in the global allowlist were changed.

Guest portal APIs are intentionally usable by anon with a valid portal token; a Supabase user JWT alone is not the portal credential. A legacy-Supabase-JWT denial case is not used as the acceptance criterion for this guest-token classification.
Per-RPC cross-participant coverage is recorded above; do not interpret a token-derived self-only API as having arbitrary target-IDOR coverage.

followUpFindings.description: The legacy Production implementation derived the indexed selector from only the first eight temporary-password characters (24 bits), creating a significant collision risk at the planned participant scale. A dedicated zero-start-only migration now derives a 64-bit selector from the first 18 trimmed characters of newly generated 24-character passwords (SK plus 22 hex characters); the final six characters remain bcrypt-verified.
followUpFindings.securityImpact: The original finding was an availability/provisioning-integrity risk, not a demonstrated authentication bypass. The replacement retains bcrypt verification and the five-failure/15-minute lockout by resolving the credential row using the 64-bit selector before checking the secret suffix.
followUpFindings.nextRequiredWork: Apply the merged migration only as part of the separately authorized zero-start Production DB2 cutover, after all other GO gates are complete. Its preflight rejects any non-empty collective_portal_credentials table. Do not execute it independently or against a populated credential set.

validation.runtimeRegression: 5,000 synthetic selectors, same-prefix two-participant login, wrong-suffix lockout and cross-account isolation passed on the rollback-only disposable restore
